full_judgment: 9. The contemner alleged that he did not receive the orders of the Magistrate passed on different dates and communicated to him as stated in the report of the Magistrate or they did not reach him except the last order. He alleged that "either the orders were misplaced by the then Thana Duty officer or those orders were not at all dispatched by the Upazilla court's Bench Clerk." On a perusal of the records of C. R. Case No. 111 of 1985 under sections 323/326/307 and 109 of the Penal Code, it appears that Memo. numbers and the dates on which the orders of the learned Magistrate were sent to the officer-in-Charge, Sailkupa, are noted against each and every order. The learned Magistrate also stated in his report that those orders were communicated to the Officer-in-Charge, Sailkupa, giving the Memo. numbers and the dates. The report of the learned Magistrate is based on record and the order-sheet. Both the court and the Thana are at the same place namely Sailkupa. Thus, prima facie, it is evident that the orders were communicated to the contemner from the court of the learned Magistrate and the presumption of service of the orders on the contemner under section 114(e) (f) of the Evidence Act is also there. The contemner alleged that the orders were misplaced by the then Thana Duty Officer. The question of misplacement arises only after the receipt of the orders from the court. We offered an option to the contemner that if he contends that the orders were not received by him then he might adduce evidence to prove the fact as the non-receipt of the orders would exonerate him from the charge, but the contemner declined to take that opportunity or chance. Thus, we are of opinion that the orders of the learned Magistrate really reached the contemner. The contemner also did not examines the Duty Officer to say that the orders received from the court were misplaced. Thus, there is no shadow of doubt is our mind that the different orders of the learned Magistrate reached the contemner in time. But he did not care to send the Magistrate any reply, intimating his difficulties if any, for non-compliance or delayed compliance of the orders of the learned Magistrate. Thus, it is clear that the contemner has willingly and intentionally avoided, evaded, flouted and disobeyed the order of the learned Magistrate. Not only that, he has added an insult to the injury by the reply to the last Memo No. 382 dated 30.6.85 by which the copy of the Magistrate's order dated 25.6.84 was communicated to him.
